items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: when I was working with Roy in Chicago, two musicians came from Memphis. One was Tony D'Amico, I believe. He's a pianist, very fine pianist... And they used to come to the Three Deuces and see us all the time.

ctx.x: She played very fine piano. But she was like a very -- she was an unusual woman. She was a highly intelligent woman, and she was governess for say like the big, rich families. I mean, a governess. Dietician, you know. And when she was in her late sixties she decided that she wanted to work at the post office, and she took the exams and they never knew -- she was such an agile woman, and such fine physical condition they never knew how old she was. So she worked there until she got out. I think she worked there…

Well, now, when I was working with Roy in Chicago, two musicians came from Memphis. One was Tony D'Amico, I believe. He's a pianist, very fine pianist and Mike Bryan, a guitarist. And they used to come to the Three Deuces and see us all the time. When we went to New York they had preceded us, they were already in New York. We went to work on the street, and Mike Bryan was a very fine guitarist. He played in the Van Epps vein. And they had moved -- they had an apartment right up the street from the Kelly's…
